skill: Identify Bernoulli differential equations by normalizing the derivative coefficient and checking for a linear-in-y term and one power-of-y term with x-only coefficients, using the source convention requiring the linear term.
reasoning_steps: Divide by any displayed coefficient of y prime, including powers of y, on a suitable nonzero domain.
Inspect normalized dependence on y: the left nonderivative term must be p(x)y and the right term q(x)y^n for a real constant n.
Distinguish x-functions from nonpower functions of y and compare powers after normalization.
Classify every offered equation, then select its subset through the original radio bank or independent checkbox fields. No solving or integrating is required.

response_contract.radio: One text-valued subset choice from the complete observed bank.
response_contract.checkbox: Boolean choice for each displayed equation; None of the above, where present, is true exactly when no equation qualifies.

difficulty: Easy examples already have unit derivative coefficient; moderate includes division by y powers. Canonical example also illustrates division by x and y. Preserve simple recognition workload, not ODE solving.
invariants: Three candidate equations in observed questions.
The Bernoulli classification depends on normalized y dependence, not label, position, sign, or x coefficient.
Use source convention that absence of p(x)y makes a candidate nonqualifying, even though the broader mathematical definition can allow p=0.
n is any real number in the lesson; no evidence supports imposing n != 0,1 as an instructional requirement.
Retain radio and checkbox source families with complete banks and None-of-above semantics.
permitted_variations: Vary x-only coefficient functions, signs, simple real powers of y, and nonpower distractors within observed complexity.
Change which candidate positions qualify and how many qualify, including none and all where the response bank supports it.
For a fixed representation, change an exponent or y-dependence so the classification changes, then derive key and explanation.
Reorder candidates and choice-bank positions without changing the underlying equation classification.
